links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM outputs across 10 repeated analyses of the same reports
links.effect: GPT-4 replicated the exact same results in 76% of reports across 10 repeated analyses, compared to 59% for GPT-3.5, indicating nondeterministic output.
links.quote: GPT-4 showed greater consistency, replicating the exact same results in 76% of the reports across 10 repeated analyses, compared to 59% for GPT-3.5, indicating more stable and reliable performance.

links.outcome: LLM performance versus specialist physicians on comorbidity extraction from the same reports
links.effect: GPT-3.5 slightly lower than physicians (McNemar P=.79); GPT-4 superior on key metrics (P<.001), sensitivity 96.8% vs 88.8% for physicians; physicians marginally better precision (97.7% vs 96.8%).
links.quote: GPT-4 demonstrated clear superiority in several key metrics (McNemar test, P<.001).

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the performance and error patterns of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 in extracting comorbidities from clinical notes compared with human oncology specialists, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
